article.title: A / An / The — when to use which
article.description: 'A/an' introduces something for the first time or something non-specific: 'I saw a dog.' 'The' refers to something already mentioned or uniquely known: 'The dog was barking.' Use 'an' before vowel SOUNDS (not just vowel letters): 'an hour' (silent h), but 'a university' (starts with a 'yoo' sound). Common mistake: 'a hour' instead of 'an hour'.

generated.caption:
Confused about 'a', 'an', or 'the'? 🤔 It's simpler than you think!

Use 'a'/'an' for new or non-specific things ('I saw a dog'). Use 'the' for something already mentioned or unique ('The dog was barking'). And remember, 'an' is for vowel *sounds*, like 'an hour' (not 'a hour'!).

slides.headlineRest: — The Ultimate Guide to Using Articles Correctly
slides.body: When introducing something for the first time or something non-specific, we use 'a' or 'an'. For example, 'I saw a dog.' On the other hand, 'the' refers to something already mentioned or uniquely known, as in 'The dog was barking.' It's also important to use 'an' before vowel sounds, not just vowel letters, so we say 'an hour' but 'a university'. A common mistake is using 'a hour' instead of 'an hour', so remember to choose the correct article based on the sound that follows.
